'''''Magnolia dealbata''''' is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Magnoliaceae]], native to Mexico. It is known commonly as the '''cloudforest magnolia'''<ref>{{PLANTS|id=MADE6|taxon=Magnolia dealbata|accessdate=28 June 2015}}</ref> and '''''eloxochitl'''''.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Pattison |first=Graham |date=18 October 2022 |title=''Magnolia dealbata'' |url=https://magnoliasociety.org/resources/Journal/Images/1973-1985_VOL_09-21/VOLUME%2021%20No.%202_19-20_MAGNOLIA%20DEALBATA_GRAHAM%20PATTISON.pdf |website=Magnolia Society}}</ref> It is sometimes considered to be a subspecies of ''[[Magnolia macrophylla]],'' which is otherwise native to the southeastern United States.<ref name= iucn/>

==Description==
''Magnolia dealbata'' is a deciduous tree, growing to average heights of 25 m tall.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Corral-Aguirre |first1=Juan |last2=Sánchez-Velásquez |first2=Lázaro Rafae |date=12 April 2006 |title=Seed ecology and germination treatments in Magnolia dealbata: An endangered species |journal=Flora - Morphology, Distribution, Functional Ecology of Plants |volume=201 |issue=3 |pages=227–232 |doi=10.1016/j.flora.2005.07.004 |bibcode=2006FMDFE.201..227C }}</ref> Larger individuals can reach 40–50 m in height.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Grímsson |first1=Friđgeir |last2=Meller |first2=Barbara |last3=Bouchal |first3=Johannes M. |last4=Zetter |first4=Reinhard |title=Combined LM and SEM study of the middle Miocene (Sarmatian) palynoflora from the Lavanttal Basin, Austria: part III. Magnoliophyta 1 – Magnoliales to Fabales |journal=Grana |date=3 April 2015 |volume=54 |issue=2 |pages=85–128 |doi=10.1080/00173134.2015.1007081 |bibcode=2015Grana..54...85G }}</ref> The flowers are large and white up to 20 cm long. The leaves are broad, reaching 60 cm length.<ref name=":1" /> The most critical difference between ''M. dealbata'' and ''[[Magnolia macrophylla]]'' is that ''M. macrophylla'' has 50 to 80 carpels in its fruit, while ''M. dealbata'' has 80 to 105, with no overlap of the numbers.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Vázquez-García | first1=José Antonio | last2=Domínguez-Yescas | first2=Reyna | last3=Pedraza-Ruiz | first3=Roberto | last4=Sánchez-González | first4=Arturo | last5=Muñiz-Castro | first5=Miguel Ángel | title=''Magnolia rzedowskiana'' (Magnoliaceae), una especie nueva de la sección Macrophylla de la parte central de la sierra Madre Oriental, México | journal=Acta botánica mexicana | publisher=Instituto de Ecología A.C., Centro Regional del Bajío | issue=112 | date=1990-01-06 | issn=0187-7151 | pages=19–36 | url=https://www.scielo.org.mx/scielo.php?script=sci_arttext&pid=S0187-71512015000300003 | language=es | access-date=2025-08-31}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
This species is [[endemic]] to [[cloud forest]]s in the [[Sierra Madre de Oaxaca]] of northern [[Oaxaca]] in eastern [[Mexico]], where it ranges from 600 and 1,900 m elevation. More than ten subpopulations have been observed, and the species' estimated [[extent of occurrence]] is 2,750 to 3,000 km<sup>2</sup>. The largest population includes over a thousand trees.<ref name = iucn/>

It grows in humid montane cloud forests, alongside ''[[Magnolia oaxacensis]]'', ''[[Pinus chiapensis]]'', ''[[Quercus laurina]]'', ''[[Liquidambar styraciflua]]'', and ''[[Clethra]]'' sp.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=iucn/>

The [[IUCN Red List]] considers populations identified as ''M. dealbata'' in the [[Sierra Madre Oriental]] of Querétaro, Veracruz, Hidalgo, Nuevo Leon, Tamaulipas and San Luis Potosí to belong to recently-described species including ''[[Magnolia nuevoleonensis]]'', ''[[Magnolia rzedowskiana]]'', and ''[[Magnolia vovidesii]]''.<ref name = iucn/> [[Plants of the World Online]] considers these synonyms of ''M. dealbata''.<ref name = powo/>

The species was once thought to be extinct until being rediscovered in 1977.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Vovides |first1=Andrew P. |last2=Iglesias |first2=Carlos G. |title=Seed Germination of Magnolia dealbata Zucc. (Magnoliaceae), An Endangered Species from Mexico |journal=HortScience |date=September 1996 |volume=31 |issue=5 |page=877 |doi=10.21273/HORTSCI.31.5.877 }}</ref>

== Etymology ==
The name '''''eloxochitl''''' was given to the tree by the [[Aztecs]]. It is derived from the [[Nahuatl]] word elotl meaning "green ear of corn", and xochitl meaning "flower".<ref name=":0" />

== Uses ==
''Magnolia dealbata'' is cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]], used as a flowering tree in [[garden]]s. It is also used for timber, and as a traditional [[medicinal plant]] for heart conditions, asthma, and stomach pain.<ref name="iucn" /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mata-Rosas |first1=Martín |last2=Jiménez-Rodríguez |first2=Ángel |last3=Chávez-Avila |first3=Victor M. |title=Somatic Embryogenesis and Organogenesis in Magnolia dealbata Zucc. (Magnoliaceae), an Endangered, Endemic Mexican Species |journal=HortScience |date=August 2006 |volume=41 |issue=5 |pages=1325–1329 |doi=10.21273/HORTSCI.41.5.1325 |doi-access=free }}</ref> The flowers are used as decorations for spiritual and cultural events.<ref name="iucn" />
